text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE FIRED: dedicated-cluster-high-p99-latency (tenant=acropolis-corp)
incident-bot: trigger=latency_p99>1200ms over 5m, affected_routes=3, error_rate_up=false
pagerduty: Escalation: page to primary on-call (raj)
raj: ack — looking
raj: anyone seen customer-side config changes?
ben-cs: acropolis reported timeouts in their app around 17:09 UTC, just FYI — they said retries started piling up
raj: ok checking metrics. p95/99 spikes on their dedicated pool. initial signs: KV cache hit rate dropped ~30% around 17:08. throughput steady, but queue depth increased.
olivia-platform: adding logs from the cluster control plane: 
```
I0321 17:07:58.123 controller.go:212] tenant=acropolis-corp pool=dedicated-4 queue_depth=92 inflight=64 p99=1580ms
I0321 17:08:12.447 scheduler.go:88] tenant=acropolis-corp alloc_fail_rate=0.03 reserved_capacity_util=0.98
```
raj: reserved_capacity_util 98% — looks like reserved pool saturated, eviction latency in tail. Could be burst queueing. Anyone running scheduled batch jobs?
maria: not that I know of, but we had a model-rollout to this tenant yesterday — but rollout was to a variant with same footprint.
tim-sre: I'm pulling kernel and GPU metrics. NVLink contended? mem high?
raj: quick mitigation options: 1) enable tenant burst-capacity (add burst nodes) 2) temporarily route acropolis traffic to hosted fallback model variant 3) increase concurrency limit per-worker to reduce queue depth (risky)
raj: @olivia-platform can you check routing policy for acropolis? whether fallback to hosted is allowed in their tenant policy (IIRC they opted into cross-tier fallback)
olivia-platform: they are allowed to fallback to hosted. I can flip routing to hosted variant for critical routes.
ben-cs: if we fallback, we should message them ASAP that latency will change. want to limit toggles if it affects SLAs.
incident-bot: pagerduty: page acknowledged by raj at 1778003336
raj: ok I'm going to enable burst nodes now and open a temporary fallback route for chat/generate endpoints only. will monitor.
raj: command run: `infractl tenant scale-burst --tenant acropolis-corp --add 2`
raj: logs after scale: 
```
I0321 17:09:34.009 scale.go:102] tenant=acropolis-corp adding_burst_nodes=2 new_reserved_util=0.84
I0321 17:09:58.212 router.go:311] tenant=acropolis-corp route_override=hosted-llm-generic for endpoints=[/v1/chat,/v1/generate]
```
maria: seeing p99 drop from ~1500ms to ~300ms on the affected routes within 40s of the change. queue depth down to 12. KV cache warming still ongoing.
ben-cs: customer says error rate dropped to negligible, their app recovered. They asked what happened and whether this will repeat.
raj: immediate mitigation succeeded. Next steps: 1) keep burst nodes for 20m 2) monitor for recurrence and root cause (why reserved pool spiked) 3) postmortem and customer note. Assigning owners.
raj: tim, can you follow GPU/memory contended metrics to rule out hardware degradation?
tim-sre: on it, dumping device metrics now.
tim-sre: GPU mem pressure normal, SM utilization ~72%. No ECC errors. Network egress on that AZ slightly higher but within limits.
maria: I'll pull scheduler logs to see if allocation churn or a hot prefix caused cache drop.
raj: ben, can you draft an initial customer message saying we had transient saturation in their reserved pool and we routed traffic to hosted while we stabilized. reassure no data exposure and we're investigating. I'll review.
ben-cs: will draft. sending first note to customer at 17:15 UTC.
incident-bot: pagerduty: escalation to secondary (maria) in 8m — please ack before handoff
maria: ack — taking over incident at 17:20 UTC. summary for handoff: burst nodes added, hosted fallback enabled for /chat,/generate, latency back to normal, waiting on scheduler logs for root cause.
raj: handing off monitoring/chat to maria, I'll stay available for questions. shifting to status update cadence every 10m.
maria: quick finding: scheduler logs show increased allocation churn from a backend tuning job on acropolis side that started at 17:06 and caused many short-lived model sessions, which hurt KV cache locality. I'm seeing many short sessions: `session_start` spikes to 1.2k/min for acropolis.
maria: recommendation: we should consider a soft rate-limit per-tenant session-start to protect the reserved pool, and add a cache-warming path for new sessions to prefetch common prefixes.
olivia-platform: filed task INF-1428 to add session-start rate limiting for reserved pools, tagging for P2.
raj: good. timeline:
- 17:07:58 trigger: p99 > 1200ms
- 17:08:12 reserved_util hit 98%
- 17:09:34 burst add +2 nodes
- 17:09:58 routing override to hosted for critical endpoints
- 17:10:40 p99 back to ~300ms
- 17:15:00 customer notified
- 17:20:00 handoff to maria
raj: incident classification: Sev-2 (customer impact, degraded latency, recovered via mitigation)
ben-cs: customer accepted explanation and wants to be informed when permanent fix is scheduled.
maria: I'll own the postmortem, will collect logs, query KV cache heatmaps, and propose mitigations. assigning to eng-runtime and eng-platform for follow-ups.
incident-bot: Incident resolved note queued — please confirm closure in thread once all follow-ups captured
raj: confirming we can close the on-call page. leaving follow-ups in INF-1428 + PM notes.
maria: closing — will schedule a 1-hour postmortem sync tomorrow 10:00 UTC. add participants: raj, tim, olivia, runtime eng lead.
ben-cs: thanks team, customer is satisfied for now. please ping me when postmortem is scheduled so I can update customer. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: incident closed (resolved_by=maria)
